color : #fff!important; } .cat-links .at-cat-item-78005:hover{ background: #2d2d2d!important; color : #fff!important; } Skip to content Home About The Michael Patrick Leahy Show Jobs Covenant School Shooting Lawfare DONATE ‘Dismantling DEI Departments Act’ Clears First Committee in Tennessee House Lawmakers in the Tennessee House of Representatives on Tuesday advanced legislation that would dismantle any Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) office or initiative in Tennessee’s state government, ban future DEI efforts, and nullify all existing contracts or agreements related to DEI.
The Dismantling DEI Departments Act, introduced as House Bill (HB) 923 by State Representative Aron Maberry (R-Clarksville) in the Tennessee State House of Representatives, would amend state law to expressly forbid any “department, agency, or other unit of state government,” from creating, authorizing, or maintaining “an office or department that promotes or requires discriminatory preferences in an effort to increase diversity, equity, or inclusion.”
It also would void all existing “mandates, policies, programs, activities, guidance, regulations, enforcement actions, consent orders, or other declarations” made by or with a state DEI authority.
HB 923 would prohibit DEI units in state government departments and agencies, county governments, municipal governments, metropolitan governments, and public colleges and universities from creating DEI offices or pushing DEI mandates.
Submitted in February, HB 923 was advanced from the committee with six votes in favor and two against.
Senate Bill 1084, by Senate Majority Leader Jack Johnson (R-Franklin), is the version of the Dismantling DEI Departments Act under consideration in the State Senate. The State and Local Government Committee is scheduled to consider it on Monday.
DEI positions exist throughout Tennessee, including in Nashville, where the Metro Council voted in 2020 to establish the new offices of “Chief Diversity Equity and Inclusion Officer” and “Workplace Diversity Manager for Social Justice.” The city anticipated that those hired for the new positions would earn in excess of $100,000 per year.
The legislation comes amid a federal crackdown by the Trump administration against DEI, which includes executive orders aimed at stripping funding from colleges and universities pushing the controversial ideology. In the wake of one executive order signed by President Donald Trump, Vanderbilt University purged its DEI web page.
Trump’s attempt to stifle DEI has reportedly led to fundraising shortfalls for nonprofits as major companies pull back from controversial sponsorships.
